1.explanation:
All of the logic for rendering the tab content and applying CSS modifiers lives in the Tab and Tabs components. Currently, none of the Tab variants destructure or render the new `renderIcon` prop, and the Tabs container never checks for an icon-only variant to apply the proper modifier class for spacing and styling. We need to
1. Update Tab.js (classic) to accept and render `renderIcon` when provided, falling back to `label` otherwise.
2. Update next/Tab.js to do the same in the function component.
3. Update next/ContainedTab.js so contained tabs support icon-only.
4. Update next/Tabs.js to detect when all children are icon-only and add an `--icon-only` CSS modifier to the nav container so the SCSS can apply the 48 px spacing and variant styles for both line and contained variants.
1.bug_scenario: The two reference images show the desired “icon-only” tabs in both the contained and line variants. Each tab should render only an icon (no text label), sized 20×20 px, with 48 px between tab centers. For the contained variant the background and outline match the “container” style, and for the line variant there is only the bottom underline indicator. In both cases, passing a renderIcon prop to <Tab> should display the icon, and Tabs (and ContainedTabs) must detect the icon-only children to add the proper CSS modifiers (e.g. `--icon-only`) to space and style the tabs correctly.
